objections.claim: E6 specifies two contradictory authoritative qualification algorithms at candidate sha256:97cd2efc59d32c8b29ca507670fbaf70bd44e3673a6d0088dcf6ca4f3d3996ad: K=12 randomly drawn mutations/fixtures, and later exhaustive execution of every element in each closed mutation and conforming-variant domain. For domains larger than 12, the sampled path can miss a lookup-table exception and produce a run-dependent qualification verdict; for domains smaller than 12, twelve independent distinct draws may be impossible. Remove sampling from the authoritative path and require enumeration of every domain/family member; retain randomized draws only in the explicitly non-authoritative dev mode, with regressions proving domains above and below 12 cannot select the sampled interpretation.

The immutable-release deletion recovery is internally unsatisfiable at candidate sha256:97cd2efc59d32c8b29ca507670fbaf70bd44e3673a6d0088dcf6ca4f3d3996ad. It promises byte-identical v0.3.0 artifacts under successor tag v0.3.1, but the source tarball embeds RELEASE-IDENTITY.tag/product_version=v0.3.0 and the CLI package/product-version remain 0.3.0; relabeling those bytes as v0.3.1 violates the lockstep version and artifact-identity contract, while changing them destroys byte identity and requires a new commit/build. Further, RELEASE-ACCEPTANCE signs only release_commit and plan_ref, so a supposedly fresh acceptance for the same commit cannot bind the successor tag or referenced incident. Define either a newly versioned accepted recovery commit and rebuilt artifacts, or a distinct signed recovery envelope binding retired tag, successor locator, incident id, and exact escrowed artifact digests without claiming the artifacts are v0.3.1; add a consumer-facing identity regression.

The local-single-user carve-out remains non-discriminating at candidate sha256:97cd2efc59d32c8b29ca507670fbaf70bd44e3673a6d0088dcf6ca4f3d3996ad. Enumerating the CLI's transitive import/spawn closure proves which files are reachable, not that those files cannot open a listener: an already-enumerated module can reach node:net/node:http/node:dgram through aliases, process.getBuiltinModule, dynamic property access, eval, or an allowed child command without adding an unresolved closure edge. Specify a closed listener-capability grammar that rejects every ambiguous/dynamic acquisition path and constrains spawned executables, or use an enforceable runtime boundary; require adversarial indirect-listener and spawned-helper fixtures that the oracle must reject.
